content_warning: Use only for study and supervised laboratory record preparation. Hypothetical examples are never actual observations. Teacher review remains outstanding.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Detecting the main classes of biological food molecules
activities.principle: Distinct classes of biomolecules give characteristic responses in appropriate laboratory identification tests; reducing and non-reducing sugars must not be conflated.
activities.record_guidance: For every labelled sample, record the initial appearance, the qualitative test performed by the teacher and the final appearance.
activities.analysis_guidance: A positive indicator supports a particular class of substance; a negative result cannot prove complete absence without suitable controls.
activities.common_error: A colour change is evidence only when the sample, reagent and control are correctly identified.
activities.recall_question: Why is a control sample helpful?
activities.recall_answer: It shows the background response so the test result can be interpreted more confidently.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Light microscope: parts, magnification and focusing
activities.principle: Total magnification equals eyepiece magnification multiplied by objective magnification; resolution is different from magnification.
activities.record_guidance: Record the microscope components identified, slide label, objective used and a labelled biological drawing.
activities.analysis_guidance: Begin interpretation by describing visible structures; do not label structures that cannot be resolved.
activities.common_error: Do not add unobserved organelles to a light-microscope drawing.
activities.recall_question: What is the total magnification with a 10x eyepiece and 40x objective?
activities.recall_answer: 400x; this does not state the resolution.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Reading electron micrographs of cell components
activities.principle: Electron micrographs reveal ultrastructure; scale bars must be used to infer real size rather than guessing from the image.
activities.record_guidance: Record specimen, visible organelles, labelled features and supplied scale-bar information.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate membranes and subcellular organization to function, while distinguishing TEM from SEM views.
activities.common_error: An enlarged photograph is not evidence of the object's actual size without a scale.
activities.recall_question: How is true size estimated from a micrograph?
activities.recall_answer: True size = measured image size divided by magnification, using consistent units.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Recognising stages of mitosis and meiosis
activities.principle: Chromosome arrangement and separation identify division stages; meiosis produces haploid products through two divisions.
activities.record_guidance: Draw one stage from each labelled slide and list visible chromosome or spindle features.
activities.analysis_guidance: Mitosis separates sister chromatids; homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis I and sister chromatids in meiosis II.
activities.common_error: Do not confuse the separation of homologues with sister chromatids.
activities.recall_question: What separates at anaphase I of meiosis?
activities.recall_answer: Homologous chromosomes separate; centromeres typically remain intact.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Amylase activity and temperature
activities.principle: Temperature changes enzyme-catalysed reaction rates; excessive heat may disrupt the active site's shape.
activities.record_guidance: Record the tested temperatures, comparable reaction endpoints and conditions held constant.
activities.analysis_guidance: Interpret the fastest effective condition within the actual tested range rather than claiming a universal optimum.
activities.common_error: A higher temperature does not always mean a faster enzyme reaction.
activities.recall_question: Why must reaction time and enzyme concentration be controlled?
activities.recall_answer: Otherwise changes in the observed rate cannot be attributed to temperature alone.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Estimating photosynthesis via oxygen output
activities.principle: Under suitable conditions oxygen evolution can act as an indirect indicator of photosynthetic activity.
activities.record_guidance: Record the light conditions, recorded oxygen amounts, timing and any instrumental limits reported in class.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relative oxygen output compares conditions only if organism size and relevant environmental factors are controlled.
activities.common_error: Oxygen output is a proxy, not a direct measure of all carbon fixed.
activities.recall_question: Name two factors that can alter photosynthetic rate.
activities.recall_answer: Light intensity and carbon dioxide availability; temperature can also matter.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: C3 versus C4 leaf cross-sections
activities.principle: Some C4 leaves have conspicuous bundle sheath chloroplasts (Kranz anatomy); C3 and C4 anatomy differ in common textbook examples.
activities.record_guidance: Draw and label the veins, mesophyll and bundle-sheath region from approved sections.
activities.analysis_guidance: Connect C4 anatomical specialization with spatial separation of initial carbon fixation and Calvin-cycle reactions.
activities.common_error: Not every specimen can be categorised from a single unclear section.
activities.recall_question: What is characteristic of many C4 leaf sections?
activities.recall_answer: Prominent chloroplast-containing bundle-sheath cells arranged around vascular bundles.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Seed respiration and respiratory quotient
activities.principle: Respiratory quotient (RQ) is CO2 produced divided by O2 consumed; its value depends on the metabolic substrate and conditions.
activities.record_guidance: Record the apparatus readouts, time and any corrections specified by the instructor.
activities.analysis_guidance: An RQ close to 1 can be consistent with predominant carbohydrate oxidation; interpretation requires experimental context.
activities.common_error: RQ is a ratio, not a rate, and measured values can include experimental errors.
activities.recall_question: What is the definition of RQ?
activities.recall_answer: RQ = volume (or molar amount) of CO2 produced / O2 consumed.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Bacteria and cyanobacteria in light micrographs
activities.principle: Bacteria and cyanobacteria are prokaryotic; cyanobacteria can be photosynthetic but lack chloroplasts.
activities.record_guidance: Record cell morphology, grouping and any visible pigmentation from prepared teaching samples.
activities.analysis_guidance: Differentiate observation of cellular shape from identification to a species.
activities.common_error: Do not claim a nucleus is present in a typical bacterial cell.
activities.recall_question: Do cyanobacteria possess chloroplasts?
activities.recall_answer: No; photosynthetic pigments are associated with internal membrane systems.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Interpreting electron images of prokaryotes
activities.principle: Electron images can show cell envelopes, cytoplasmic content and certain external structures depending on preparation.
activities.record_guidance: Use scale bars and clear labels to identify only resolvable structures.
activities.analysis_guidance: Infer likely roles of an observed surface or internal feature without asserting structures absent from the image.
activities.common_error: A proposed function must be distinguished from a directly visible structure.
activities.recall_question: Why is an electron micrograph useful here?
activities.recall_answer: It can reveal structures much smaller than those resolved using light microscopy.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Comparing selected protists and algae
activities.principle: Common examples show contrasting movement, cell organization and body forms, from unicells to multicellular algae.
activities.record_guidance: Make labelled sketches of the specimens shown and identify movement or morphology where observed.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use combinations of features to compare Euglena, Amoeba, Paramecium and named algal groups.
activities.common_error: A single feature like green colour is not sufficient to classify every organism.
activities.recall_question: How does Amoeba typically move?
activities.recall_answer: By temporary cytoplasmic extensions called pseudopodia.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Recognising major groups of plants
activities.principle: Bryophyte-like, fern-like, gymnosperm and flowering-plant groups differ in vascular tissues and reproduction.
activities.record_guidance: Record representative examples and readily identifiable reproductive structures.
activities.analysis_guidance: Distinguish seed-bearing from spore-producing representatives and note presence of flowers or cones.
activities.common_error: Do not describe every bryophyte as having true roots.
activities.recall_question: What distinguishes angiosperms from gymnosperms?
activities.recall_answer: Angiosperm ovules are enclosed within carpels; gymnosperm ovules are exposed.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Recognising selected fungal groups
activities.principle: Fungi are heterotrophs with absorptive nutrition; reproductive structures support comparison of named groups.
activities.record_guidance: Describe the hyphae or reproductive structures seen in authorised preserved images or slides.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use reproductive morphology cautiously; many species require more evidence for identification.
activities.common_error: Do not equate all fungal filaments with plant roots.
activities.recall_question: Are fungi autotrophic like green plants?
activities.recall_answer: No; they obtain nutrients by absorption from organic sources.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Distinguishing major invertebrate phyla
activities.principle: Body symmetry, segmentation, appendages and special structural features help classify animal phyla.
activities.record_guidance: Record observations from specimens/models of cnidarians, flatworms, nematodes, annelids, molluscs, arthropods and echinoderms.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use multiple diagnostic characteristics rather than one superficial resemblance.
activities.common_error: Radial adult echinoderms are not identical in body plan to cnidarians.
activities.recall_question: Which group has a jointed exoskeleton?
activities.recall_answer: Arthropoda.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Comparing the main vertebrate groups
activities.principle: Typical fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals have distinguishing body coverings and reproductive adaptations.
activities.record_guidance: Record visible traits from safe specimens/models and label the correct taxonomic group.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use a set of traits; avoid simplistic single-trait absolute rules.
activities.common_error: Not every mammal gives birth to live young.
activities.recall_question: What is a typical defining feature of mammals?
activities.recall_answer: Mammary glands that produce milk for offspring.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Cell types in plant tissues
activities.principle: Meristematic and differentiated tissues have distinctive cell walls, shapes and functions.
activities.record_guidance: Draw representative prepared cells of epidermis, parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma or conducting tissues as presented.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate wall thickness, living status and shape to support, transport and storage.
activities.common_error: Avoid confusing lignified xylem elements with phloem sieve elements.
activities.recall_question: Why are many xylem vessel elements hollow at maturity?
activities.recall_answer: The absence of living contents helps form continuous conduits for water transport.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Monocot and dicot root/stem cross-sections
activities.principle: Primary stem and root arrangements of xylem, phloem and ground tissue differ among typical monocots and dicots.
activities.record_guidance: Record each specimen's vascular pattern and draw a labelled cross-section.
activities.analysis_guidance: An organised ring of vascular bundles is typical of a young dicot stem; scattered bundles are typical of many monocot stems.
activities.common_error: Do not confuse a stem cross-section with a root cross-section.
activities.recall_question: What typically distinguishes a dicot root vascular core?
activities.recall_answer: Xylem often forms a central star-like pattern with phloem between its arms.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Secondary growth and woody tissues
activities.principle: Vascular cambium makes secondary xylem towards the inside and secondary phloem towards the outside.
activities.record_guidance: Sketch growth rings where visible and identify secondary xylem, rays and outer tissues.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate the tissue organization to mechanical support and transport.
activities.common_error: Not all visible bands can be assigned an exact year without environmental context.
activities.recall_question: What produces secondary xylem?
activities.recall_answer: The vascular cambium.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Stomata and lenticels
activities.principle: Stomata regulate gas exchange via guard-cell aperture changes; lenticels facilitate gas diffusion through protective tissues.
activities.record_guidance: Record the observed stomatal form, location and any lenticel features from approved specimens.
activities.analysis_guidance: Describe anatomical evidence and link openings to gas exchange, not direct measurements of flux.
activities.common_error: A stomatal opening alone does not establish transpiration rate.
activities.recall_question: What controls the pore opening in a stoma?
activities.recall_answer: Changes in guard-cell turgor and associated wall mechanics.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Epidermal-cell solute potential study
activities.principle: Plasmolysis indicates loss of water from cells in a more concentrated external solution; incipient plasmolysis helps estimate cell sap properties.
activities.record_guidance: Record the external solution labels and fractions of cells showing the diagnostic appearance.
activities.analysis_guidance: Interpret a threshold cautiously; concentration and water potential must not be used as interchangeable units.
activities.common_error: Cell membrane withdrawal is not the same as shrinkage of the rigid cell wall.
activities.recall_question: What is incipient plasmolysis?
activities.recall_answer: The initial stage at which the plasma membrane begins to detach from the cell wall.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Estimating tissue water potential with strips
activities.principle: Water moves according to water-potential gradients; no net mass or length change may identify an approximately isotonic condition.
activities.record_guidance: Record before-and-after masses or lengths and calculate percentage change where appropriate.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot percentage change against external condition; an estimated zero crossing is an approximation.
activities.common_error: Never treat raw mass change as a percentage without dividing by initial mass.
activities.recall_question: How is percentage change in mass calculated?
activities.recall_answer: 100 x (final mass - initial mass) / initial mass.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Water uptake recorded with a potometer
activities.principle: A potometer measures water uptake of a shoot, usually as a proxy for transpiration, not transpiration directly.
activities.record_guidance: Record changes of indicator position, elapsed time and environmental conditions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compare uptake per unit time; account for limitations such as water stored in the tissue.
activities.common_error: Water uptake is not exactly equivalent to evaporation at every instant.
activities.recall_question: What does a potometer measure directly?
activities.recall_answer: Water uptake by the apparatus or cut shoot under the stated conditions.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Microscopic comparison of animal tissues
activities.principle: Epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissues differ in organization and function.
activities.record_guidance: For approved prepared slides, draw representative cell shapes and organisation patterns.
activities.analysis_guidance: Justify tissue identification by features such as striation, matrix and cell arrangement.
activities.common_error: Avoid identifying a tissue from one isolated cell with no context.
activities.recall_question: Which broad tissue type transmits electrical signals?
activities.recall_answer: Nervous tissue.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Human digestive tract: anatomy and function
activities.principle: The tract and associated glands coordinate ingestion, digestion, absorption and egestion.
activities.record_guidance: On an outline model, locate and label main organs and associated glands.
activities.analysis_guidance: Connect each organ to its main function without implying digestion occurs identically throughout.
activities.common_error: Bile assists fat emulsification; it is not a digestive enzyme.
activities.recall_question: What is the principal site for nutrient absorption?
activities.recall_answer: The small intestine.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Human circulatory-system organization
activities.principle: Double circulation separates pulmonary and systemic pathways; the heart provides coordinated pumping.
activities.record_guidance: Trace the path through major chambers and vessels using a labelled diagram.
activities.analysis_guidance: Differentiate oxygenation, direction of flow and pressure; pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood.
activities.common_error: Arteries are defined by carrying blood away from the heart, not always by oxygen content.
activities.recall_question: Where does the right ventricle pump blood?
activities.recall_answer: Towards the lungs via the pulmonary trunk and arteries.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Respiratory anatomy and exercise measurements
activities.principle: Ventilation depends on pressure gradients; exercise often increases ventilation rate and pulse rate.
activities.record_guidance: Record resting and post-activity pulse/respiratory readings only during teacher-approved ordinary activity.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compare matched measures while respecting individual variation and timing.
activities.common_error: Pulse rate is not identical to respiratory rate.
activities.recall_question: What causes airflow into the lungs during normal inspiration?
activities.recall_answer: Thoracic volume rises and alveolar pressure falls below atmospheric pressure.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Animal excretory structures compared
activities.principle: Animals dispose of metabolic wastes using different structures adapted to their body plans.
activities.record_guidance: Label examples shown in approved diagrams: protonephridia, nephridia, Malpighian tubules and vertebrate kidneys.
activities.analysis_guidance: Match each structure with its major location and function.
activities.common_error: Excretion is removal of metabolic wastes; egestion is removal of undigested food.
activities.recall_question: What are Malpighian tubules associated with?
activities.recall_answer: Excretion and osmoregulation in many insects.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Organization of the human nervous system
activities.principle: The central nervous system integrates information while peripheral divisions connect it with receptors and effectors.
activities.record_guidance: Draw a hierarchical chart with CNS, PNS and appropriate subdivisions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain sensory input and motor output using a simple reflex path.
activities.common_error: Reflexes need not require conscious cerebral-cortex decisions.
activities.recall_question: Which structures form the CNS?
activities.recall_answer: Brain and spinal cord.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Sensory receptors and stimulus detection
activities.principle: Receptors transduce particular forms of stimulus energy into biological signals.
activities.record_guidance: Complete an annotated chart of major receptor types and stimuli.
activities.analysis_guidance: Distinguish receptor, sensory pathway and conscious perception.
activities.common_error: A receptor responds preferentially to an adequate stimulus, not necessarily exclusively.
activities.recall_question: What does sensory transduction mean?
activities.recall_answer: Conversion of stimulus energy into an electrical signal in a receptor system.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Human eye and ear structures
activities.principle: The eye focuses light onto a photoreceptor layer; the ear supports hearing and balance.
activities.record_guidance: Draw separate labelled outlines and annotate how structures support their functions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Trace visual and auditory stimulus pathways conceptually.
activities.common_error: The semicircular canals primarily detect head rotation, not sound.
activities.recall_question: Where is the retina found?
activities.recall_answer: It lines the inside of the eye and contains photoreceptors.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Male reproductive system: diagram study
activities.principle: The reproductive system produces, matures and transports sperm, with accessory glands contributing to seminal fluid.
activities.record_guidance: Label organs on a standard textbook diagram and add concise functions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Keep the distinction between sperm production and hormonal control clear.
activities.common_error: The urethra is not the anatomical site of sperm production.
activities.recall_question: Where is sperm production located?
activities.recall_answer: In seminiferous tubules within testes.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Female reproductive system: diagram study
activities.principle: Ovaries form oocytes and secrete hormones; the uterine tract supports fertilisation and development.
activities.record_guidance: Label a standard cross-sectional diagram and summarise each structure's role.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate ovulation, transport and implantation to the correct anatomical locations.
activities.common_error: Fertilisation usually takes place in the uterine tube, not within the ovary.
activities.recall_question: Where does implantation normally occur?
activities.recall_answer: In the uterine endometrium.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Skull and vertebral column on models
activities.principle: The axial skeleton protects nervous tissue, supports the body and permits specialised movement.
activities.record_guidance: Annotate skull regions and vertebral groups; record visible joint features.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain the shape-function relationship between vertebrae, discs and locomotion.
activities.common_error: The sacrum is made of fused vertebrae, not a single primary vertebra.
activities.recall_question: What protects the spinal cord?
activities.recall_answer: The vertebral canal formed by the vertebrae.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Appendicular skeleton and movement
activities.principle: Limb bones and girdles work with joints and muscles for manipulation and locomotion.
activities.record_guidance: Label the pectoral/pelvic girdles and major limb bones; identify principal joint types.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate long-bone structure, articulations and muscle action to movement.
activities.common_error: The thumb's opposability involves specialised articulation, not an extra finger bone.
activities.recall_question: What connects the upper limb to the axial skeleton?
activities.recall_answer: The pectoral girdle.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Sterilisation: selecting safe methods
activities.principle: Sterilisation removes or inactivates viable microorganisms; disinfection has a different purpose and may not sterilise.
activities.record_guidance: For teacher-provided demonstrations, record the equipment type, treatment category and validation evidence.
activities.analysis_guidance: Match the broad control method to the material and distinguish effectiveness from appearance.
activities.common_error: A visibly clean surface is not necessarily sterile.
activities.recall_question: What is the difference between disinfection and sterilisation?
activities.recall_answer: Sterilisation aims to eliminate all viable microbial forms; disinfection reduces harmful microorganisms.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Microbial growth medium: interpreting demonstrations
activities.principle: Appropriate nutrients and environmental conditions may support microbial growth; colonies are not equivalent to species identification.
activities.record_guidance: Only study sealed teacher-prepared demonstration plates or published photographs; note visible colony characteristics.
activities.analysis_guidance: Discuss contamination controls and the limitations of colony appearance without handling growth.
activities.common_error: Never assume an unknown culture is harmless or reopen a cultured plate.
activities.recall_question: Can colony colour alone identify a microbe?
activities.recall_answer: No; additional validated tests would be necessary.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Understanding simple staining of microbes
activities.principle: A basic stain increases contrast so cellular shapes become easier to observe in prepared microscopy slides.
activities.record_guidance: Use teacher-provided prepared slides or digital micrographs; record shape, grouping and scale where possible.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain what staining reveals and what it does not identify.
activities.common_error: A simple stain does not establish Gram reaction or precise species.
activities.recall_question: What can a simple stain show well?
activities.recall_answer: Broad cell morphology and grouping.

activities.subject: biology
activities.title: Comparing disinfectants: evidence and limitations
activities.principle: Microbial control depends on agent, concentration, exposure conditions and organism; disinfection is not synonymous with sterilisation.
activities.record_guidance: Record data supplied by the teacher or a safe case-study chart, including a control.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compare outcome measures without assuming that one finding generalises to all microbes.
activities.common_error: Do not experiment with disinfectant mixtures or uncontrolled microbial samples.
activities.recall_question: Why is an untreated control essential?
activities.recall_answer: It provides a baseline for judging the treatment effect.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Cathode-ray properties in a demonstrated apparatus
activities.principle: Cathode rays consist of negatively charged particles; their deflection provides evidence about charge and particle nature.
activities.record_guidance: Describe a teacher-provided diagram, predicted deflection and the displayed observations.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate beam direction to the sign of charge without handling high-voltage equipment.
activities.common_error: A cathode-ray tube is specialised electrical apparatus, not a home demonstration.
activities.recall_question: Which subatomic particle forms a cathode-ray beam?
activities.recall_answer: Electrons.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Molecular and ionic shapes using models
activities.principle: Electron-pair repulsion helps predict approximate molecular geometry, while lone pairs modify bond angles.
activities.record_guidance: Sketch teacher-supplied ball-and-stick models and list bonding/nonbonding pairs around the central atom.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain shapes using electron-domain geometry rather than memorising images alone.
activities.common_error: Molecular shape need not be identical to electron-pair arrangement.
activities.recall_question: What is the molecular shape of NH3?
activities.recall_answer: Trigonal pyramidal, with a lone pair on N.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Laboratory glassware, mass and measurement quality
activities.principle: Appropriate equipment selection depends on measurement purpose, uncertainty and calibration.
activities.record_guidance: Record the instrument name, smallest division, reading and unit from supervised demonstrations.
activities.analysis_guidance: Report measurements with sensible significant figures and avoid unwarranted precision.
activities.common_error: A beaker is not a substitute for volumetric glassware for accurate solution preparation.
activities.recall_question: Why note an instrument's least count?
activities.recall_answer: It helps interpret measurement precision and uncertainty.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Standard solutions: concentration calculations
activities.principle: A standard solution has a known concentration; mass, amount and volume must be kept in consistent units.
activities.record_guidance: Record labelled sample information and show calculations from given numerical data, without preparing chemicals independently.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use n = m/M and c = n/V for molar concentration when applicable.
activities.common_error: Never confuse millilitres with litres in molarity calculations.
activities.recall_question: What mass corresponds to 0.100 mol of a 58.5 g/mol substance?

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Gas molar-volume concept and measurements
activities.principle: At fixed temperature and pressure, gas amount and volume are related by the ideal-gas approximation.
activities.record_guidance: Record apparatus readings supplied by the teacher, T and P conditions and any calibration notes.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use PV = nRT in consistent units where appropriate; discuss humidity and pressure effects.
activities.common_error: Molar volume is condition-dependent, not a universal fixed number.
activities.recall_question: How does gas volume change with temperature at constant pressure and moles?
activities.recall_answer: Absolute volume is proportional to absolute temperature in the ideal approximation.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Estimating magnesium relative atomic mass from gas data
activities.principle: Stoichiometric gas production can be related to reacted magnesium mass and its amount of substance.
activities.record_guidance: Record teacher-supplied mass and gas-volume readings and the balanced reaction supplied in class.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use the mole relationship only after adjusting gas conditions and considering measurement limitations.
activities.common_error: Uncorrected gas volume may introduce systematic error.
activities.recall_question: What is the Mg:H2 mole ratio in Mg + 2H+ -> Mg2+ + H2?

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Energy changes during acid-base neutralisation
activities.principle: The observed solution-temperature change can estimate transferred heat under calorimetry assumptions.
activities.record_guidance: Record provided temperature and mass data, sign conventions and heat-loss caveats.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use q = mc(delta T) for solution heat; reaction enthalpy is interpreted with sign and mole basis.
activities.common_error: The heat gained by solution is not automatically the reaction enthalpy without a sign change.
activities.recall_question: Is typical strong acid-strong base neutralisation exothermic?
activities.recall_answer: Yes, so the enthalpy change of reaction is negative.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Using Hess's law with reaction-enthalpy data
activities.principle: Enthalpy is a state function; the net change is path independent for the same states.
activities.record_guidance: Arrange teacher-supplied reaction enthalpies in a diagram or algebraic cycle.
activities.analysis_guidance: Reverse a reaction -> reverse its enthalpy sign; multiply equation -> multiply enthalpy.
activities.common_error: Never add reaction equations without applying the same algebra to enthalpy values.
activities.recall_question: What happens to delta H when a reaction is reversed?
activities.recall_answer: Its sign changes.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Comparing s-block metal reactivity (theory only)
activities.principle: Alkali and alkaline-earth metals commonly form ionic compounds and show group trends in reactivity.
activities.record_guidance: Use teacher-authorised video or diagrams to compare general reaction patterns.
activities.analysis_guidance: Discuss effects of electron removal and hydration without attempting reactions.
activities.common_error: Reactive metals require professional handling; never reproduce demonstrations privately.
activities.recall_question: How does first ionisation energy generally vary down Group 1?
activities.recall_answer: It generally decreases.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Recognising flame-test evidence
activities.principle: Electronic excitation and relaxation may yield characteristic emission wavelengths.
activities.record_guidance: Record teacher-provided photographs or safe demonstrations and the displayed colour labels.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain why flame colours relate to emission spectra and why contamination causes confusion.
activities.common_error: Colour observed by eye alone is not a universally definitive element identification.
activities.recall_question: Which common Group 1 element is associated with an intense yellow flame?
activities.recall_answer: Sodium.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Reasoning about inorganic anions
activities.principle: Anions may be distinguished by characteristic patterns of precipitation, gas evolution and redox behaviour in approved tests.
activities.record_guidance: Read a provided observation matrix; record species hypotheses and balanced equations as homework.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use multiple independent observations to support an identification.
activities.common_error: Do not independently generate potentially toxic gases or handle analytical reagents.
activities.recall_question: Why are confirmatory tests used?
activities.recall_answer: Different ions can produce overlapping initial observations.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Nitrogen as a component of air
activities.principle: The fraction of air that does not support some common processes illustrates that oxygen is only part of air.
activities.record_guidance: Interpret teacher-provided demonstrations and air-composition charts.
activities.analysis_guidance: Approximate dry-air nitrogen content is about 78% by volume.
activities.common_error: Air contains more than oxygen and nitrogen; do not call the remainder pure nitrogen.
activities.recall_question: What gas is the major constituent of dry air?
activities.recall_answer: Nitrogen.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Distinguishing halide ions from evidence
activities.principle: Halide ions can be distinguished through appropriate confirmatory analytical patterns.
activities.record_guidance: Use assigned observation tables and name possible halides, with a teacher-provided key.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain solubility and ionic product ideas conceptually.
activities.common_error: Precipitate colours alone can be ambiguous in mixed or contaminated samples.
activities.recall_question: What charge does a halide ion normally carry?
activities.recall_answer: Minus one.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Thiosulfate standardisation calculations
activities.principle: Iodometric analysis links a known oxidant amount to iodine and subsequently to thiosulfate stoichiometry.
activities.record_guidance: Write equations and sample calculations using supplied titration data only.
activities.analysis_guidance: Separate equivalence chemistry from the visual endpoint.
activities.common_error: A titration endpoint is an indicator observation, not the exact theoretical equivalence point.
activities.recall_question: Why must stoichiometric coefficients be used in concentration calculations?
activities.recall_answer: Because equal reacting volumes do not mean equal chemical amounts.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Identifying ammonium-related observations
activities.principle: Acid-base equilibrium explains the relationship between NH4+ and NH3.
activities.record_guidance: Interpret supplied observation descriptions while distinguishing an ion in solution from released gas.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use NH4+ <=> NH3 + H+ to reason about acid-base behaviour.
activities.common_error: Ammonia is irritating; no self-directed gas generation or smelling tests.
activities.recall_question: Is aqueous NH4+ an acid or a base in the Bronsted sense?
activities.recall_answer: It can donate a proton, so it behaves as a weak acid.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Solubility of s-block salts: trends and exceptions
activities.principle: Lattice enthalpy and hydration influence solubility; simple periodic trends have exceptions.
activities.record_guidance: Record teacher-provided solubility comparisons for a named family of salts.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain trends qualitatively, noting changing ion sizes and hydration.
activities.common_error: Never memorise 'all s-block salts are soluble' as a universal rule.
activities.recall_question: Why are solubility trends not always monotonic?
activities.recall_answer: Because lattice and hydration effects compete.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Thermal stability of nitrates and carbonates
activities.principle: Thermal decomposition behaviour is influenced by cation size and polarising power.
activities.record_guidance: Use only video or teacher-provided observations of heating experiments.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compare qualitative trend with group and the size/charge of cations.
activities.common_error: Hot decomposition processes and released gases must be teacher-managed.
activities.recall_question: Why do smaller highly polarising cations often destabilise anions?
activities.recall_answer: They distort anion electron density more strongly.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Colour and ligands in transition-metal complexes
activities.principle: d-electron arrangements and ligand environment influence visible-light absorption and observed colour.
activities.record_guidance: Record image-based colour comparisons of labelled complex ions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Connect colour changes to differences in electronic energy gaps with caution.
activities.common_error: Observed colour is the light transmitted/reflected, not the absorbed colour.
activities.recall_question: What broad property makes many transition-metal complexes coloured?
activities.recall_answer: Electronic transitions can absorb parts of visible light.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Permanganate-versus-iron(II) analytical stoichiometry
activities.principle: Oxidation-reduction titration quantifies Fe2+ through a known oxidant and balanced electron transfer.
activities.record_guidance: Interpret teacher-provided titres and equations; perform calculations on paper.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use electron balance to establish the mole ratio and label concentration units.
activities.common_error: Endpoints and exact acid conditions are to be handled by trained teachers.
activities.recall_question: How many electrons does Fe2+ lose to form Fe3+?
activities.recall_answer: One electron.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Oxalate and permanganate stoichiometry
activities.principle: Permanganate and oxalate undergo electron-transfer reactions; the mole ratio depends on balanced half-equations.
activities.record_guidance: Use given half-equations and titre records to infer unknown concentration.
activities.analysis_guidance: Balance charge and atoms before computing moles.
activities.common_error: Do not guess coefficients from the colour change.
activities.recall_question: What does an oxidising agent do?
activities.recall_answer: It accepts electrons and is reduced.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Changing complex-ion equilibria: Cu, Ni, Co
activities.principle: Ligand replacement affects coordination environment and, often, colour.
activities.record_guidance: Compare teacher-supplied photographs with labelled aqueous coordination environments.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain a shift conceptually through competition between ligands and equilibrium.
activities.common_error: Colour depends on concentration, ligand identity and speciation.
activities.recall_question: What is a ligand?
activities.recall_answer: A species that donates an electron pair to form a coordinate bond.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Oxidation states of manganese in case studies
activities.principle: A transition element can possess several oxidation states with differing colours and properties.
activities.record_guidance: Classify supplied samples by the assigned Mn oxidation state and oxidation/reduction changes.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use oxidation numbers to track electron transfer, not colour alone.
activities.common_error: Treat manganese-containing solutions as supervised-lab materials, not home chemistry.
activities.recall_question: What happens to oxidation number during oxidation?
activities.recall_answer: It increases.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Recognising transition-ion patterns
activities.principle: Fe, Cu, Ni and Cr ions may exhibit differing precipitate and complex formation patterns.
activities.record_guidance: Use an authorised result chart to associate each ion with its supported evidence.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain why hydroxide precipitates and ammine complexes give complementary clues.
activities.common_error: Solubility in excess reagent is not universal for all metal hydroxides.
activities.recall_question: Why can ammonia affect a metal-ion solution in more than one way?
activities.recall_answer: It can influence hydroxide equilibria and coordinate as a ligand.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Chemical behaviour of alkenes and alkynes
activities.principle: C=C and C-triple-C bonds can undergo addition reactions; terminal alkynes have special reactivity.
activities.record_guidance: Study approved equations and teacher-supplied demonstration data.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compare a reaction category and the structural requirement for an observation.
activities.common_error: No unsupervised handling of bromine, reactive silver or copper reagents.
activities.recall_question: What makes an alkene unsaturated?
activities.recall_answer: It contains a carbon-carbon double bond.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Alcohols: comparing physical and chemical properties
activities.principle: The -OH functional group can influence intermolecular bonding and oxidation patterns.
activities.record_guidance: Compare structural formulas and teacher-provided test outcomes.
activities.analysis_guidance: Differentiate primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols for common oxidation reasoning.
activities.common_error: Do not infer that every alcohol gives an identical oxidation product.
activities.recall_question: Why can short-chain alcohols mix well with water?
activities.recall_answer: Their hydroxyl groups can hydrogen-bond with water.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Phenol: acidity and aromatic substitution
activities.principle: Phenol's conjugate base is resonance stabilised, affecting acidity relative to many ordinary alcohols.
activities.record_guidance: Evaluate assigned observation descriptions alongside structural formulas.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain the difference between phenols and aliphatic alcohols without overgeneralising.
activities.common_error: Phenol and strong analytical reagents require controlled laboratory handling.
activities.recall_question: Why is phenol generally more acidic than ethanol?
activities.recall_answer: Phenoxide is resonance stabilised more effectively than ethoxide.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Aldehydes and ketones: functional-group evidence
activities.principle: The carbonyl group has polar bonding; aldehydes and ketones can differ in their response to mild oxidation.
activities.record_guidance: Classify structures and analyse a teacher-provided qualitative-results table.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use both structural and test evidence; note exceptions and interfering compounds.
activities.common_error: One colour or precipitate is insufficient for definitive identification.
activities.recall_question: What structural feature differentiates an aldehyde from a ketone?
activities.recall_answer: An aldehyde has at least one H attached to the carbonyl carbon.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Carboxylic acids: acid-base and structural properties
activities.principle: The -COOH group can donate a proton; resonance stabilisation of carboxylate supports acidity.
activities.record_guidance: Record assigned structures, equations and given indicator or salt-forming data.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain why carboxylic acids typically form carboxylate salts with bases.
activities.common_error: Do not confuse carboxylic acids with aldehydes based on the carbonyl alone.
activities.recall_question: What is the conjugate base of ethanoic acid?
activities.recall_answer: Ethanoate, CH3COO-.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Aromatic amines: aniline case-study
activities.principle: Aniline has an amino group directly bonded to an aromatic ring, altering basicity and substitution behaviour.
activities.record_guidance: Analyse a supplied set of qualitative observations and structural questions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Reason about lone-pair delocalisation and its effect on basicity.
activities.common_error: Aniline is hazardous; use diagrams and teacher-provided evidence, not practical handling.
activities.recall_question: Why is aniline generally less basic than many aliphatic amines?
activities.recall_answer: Its nitrogen lone pair can delocalise into the aromatic ring.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Reaction rate versus acid concentration (Mg system)
activities.principle: Higher reactant concentration can alter collision frequency and observed rate when other factors are controlled.
activities.record_guidance: Plot teacher-provided rate data with labelled axes and units.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain trends with particle collisions, while recognising nonlinearity and experimental limitations.
activities.common_error: Do not confuse faster rate with a larger total product amount.
activities.recall_question: Name one control variable in a concentration-rate comparison.
activities.recall_answer: Temperature or magnesium surface area, where applicable.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Rate study with thiosulfate-related data
activities.principle: A visible endpoint can provide an indirect time-based rate measure; concentration effects can be graphed.
activities.record_guidance: Use prepared data, noting the fixed visual endpoint and time definition.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compare 1/time cautiously as a rate proxy under matched conditions.
activities.common_error: A 1/time plot is not a direct concentration-versus-time reaction rate.
activities.recall_question: Why is a fixed endpoint important?
activities.recall_answer: It makes comparisons between trials meaningful.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Rate law: Fe(III) and iodide case-study
activities.principle: Initial-rate data may reveal reaction orders that are measured experimentally rather than inferred from an overall equation.
activities.record_guidance: Use a supplied initial-rates table to compare rate changes when one concentration changes.
activities.analysis_guidance: If doubling a reactant doubles rate while others remain constant, first-order dependence is suggested.
activities.common_error: Balanced overall equation coefficients do not automatically equal kinetic orders.
activities.recall_question: How can an unknown order be estimated from initial rates?
activities.recall_answer: Compare rates for trials differing in only one starting concentration.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Dynamic equilibrium with Fe3+/thiocyanate models
activities.principle: At equilibrium forward and reverse rates are equal; concentrations need not be equal.
activities.record_guidance: Apply Le Chatelier's principle to supplied solution-colour scenarios.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain why a system shifts in response to a changed concentration.
activities.common_error: A coloured system does not stop reacting when the colour stabilises.
activities.recall_question: What is true of reaction rates at dynamic equilibrium?
activities.recall_answer: Forward and reverse rates are equal.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Temperature effects on NO2/N2O4 equilibrium (theory)
activities.principle: Temperature changes an equilibrium constant according to reaction enthalpy; gas-phase colour may provide a visual cue.
activities.record_guidance: Interpret diagrams or published data only, without generating or collecting toxic NO2.
activities.analysis_guidance: Determine the direction of the temperature shift from thermodynamic information provided.
activities.common_error: NO2 is toxic; no direct demonstration or preparation outside a managed laboratory.
activities.recall_question: Does a catalyst change the equilibrium constant?
activities.recall_answer: No; it changes the rate of approaching equilibrium.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Predicting salt-solution pH
activities.principle: Salt pH depends on acid-base properties of component ions, not simply the presence of 'salt'.
activities.record_guidance: Categorise teacher-provided pH readings or simulated values by ion hydrolysis.
activities.analysis_guidance: Link conjugate-acid and conjugate-base strengths to acidic, neutral or basic solutions.
activities.common_error: Not all aqueous salts have pH 7.
activities.recall_question: Would aqueous ammonium chloride tend to be acidic or basic?
activities.recall_answer: Acidic, because ammonium acts as a weak acid in water.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Carbonate/acid titration: endpoint interpretation
activities.principle: Carbonate neutralisation occurs in stages; indicators signal different pH ranges.
activities.record_guidance: Interpret assigned titration curves and example titres conceptually.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use neutralisation stoichiometry and distinguish indicator endpoints.
activities.common_error: The two endpoints must not be treated as chemically identical.
activities.recall_question: What is an indicator endpoint?
activities.recall_answer: The observable indicator change used to estimate an equivalence point.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Calcium hydroxide and solubility-product reasoning
activities.principle: At equilibrium, Ksp is the product of dissolved-ion activities approximated by concentrations under suitable conditions.
activities.record_guidance: Calculate Ksp from hypothetical solubility data with the correct ionic exponents.
activities.analysis_guidance: For Ca(OH)2, the idealised expression is [Ca2+][OH-]^2.
activities.common_error: Ksp is not simply equal to molar solubility.
activities.recall_question: If molar solubility is s, what is the idealised Ksp for Ca(OH)2?
activities.recall_answer: Ksp = 4s^3.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Distribution coefficient for ethanoic acid
activities.principle: A solute distributes between two immiscible phases according to equilibrium and molecular association effects.
activities.record_guidance: Interpret teacher-supplied phase-concentration data and clearly identify the ratio convention.
activities.analysis_guidance: A distribution ratio is a ratio of concentrations in specified phases at a stated temperature.
activities.common_error: A partition ratio can be concentration-dependent when association or ionisation occurs.
activities.recall_question: Why must the ratio convention be stated?
activities.recall_answer: The reciprocal gives a different numerical value.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Electrochemical series from evidence
activities.principle: Cell potentials reflect differences in reduction tendencies under specified conditions.
activities.record_guidance: Arrange metals using given cell-potential values and labelled half-cells.
activities.analysis_guidance: Distinguish oxidation at the anode and reduction at the cathode.
activities.common_error: Cathode is where reduction happens in all electrochemical cells.
activities.recall_question: What reaction occurs at the anode?
activities.recall_answer: Oxidation.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Reference electrodes and standard-potential measurement
activities.principle: Standard electrode potentials are relative; a reference half-cell enables comparisons.
activities.record_guidance: Label a teacher-supplied reference-electrode diagram and record stated standard conditions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Differentiate the electrode reaction, the role of salt bridge and voltmeter sign.
activities.common_error: A single isolated half-cell has no directly measurable absolute electrode potential.
activities.recall_question: Why are reference electrodes needed?
activities.recall_answer: They provide a reproducible comparison point for electrode potentials.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Soap formation: reaction concept and purification
activities.principle: Saponification is base hydrolysis of suitable esters, yielding carboxylate salts and alcohol components.
activities.record_guidance: Use equations, structural sketches and teacher-provided final-product descriptions only.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain amphiphilic structures and how micelles assist cleaning.
activities.common_error: Soap production involves potentially caustic conditions; do not attempt home synthesis.
activities.recall_question: What is the dual character of a soap ion?
activities.recall_answer: A hydrophilic ionic head and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Steam distillation: essential-oil concept
activities.principle: Steam distillation can help transfer volatile, water-immiscible compounds at lower bulk temperatures than some direct distillations.
activities.record_guidance: Use diagrams of apparatus and teacher-supplied distillate observations.
activities.analysis_guidance: Explain vapour-pressure contributions qualitatively.
activities.common_error: Distillation equipment uses heat and vapour; no unsupervised assembly.
activities.recall_question: Why can steam distillation be useful for heat-sensitive compounds?
activities.recall_answer: It may allow co-distillation at a reduced effective temperature.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Biodiesel: transesterification model
activities.principle: Transesterification converts suitable triglyceride esters into different esters under controlled industrial/laboratory conditions.
activities.record_guidance: Analyse molecular equations and compare feedstock/product structures.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate ester formation to changed fuel properties without trying synthesis.
activities.common_error: Biodiesel preparation may involve flammable and toxic chemicals; no independent attempt.
activities.recall_question: What type of reaction underpins conventional biodiesel production?
activities.recall_answer: Transesterification.

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Percentage ethanoic acid in vinegar: calculations
activities.principle: Acid concentration may be inferred from a standardised acid-base titration dataset.
activities.record_guidance: Use supplied sample-volume and titre data to calculate molarity and mass percentage with stated assumptions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Keep dilution factors, molar mass and volume-to-mass conversion explicit.
activities.common_error: The percentage basis (% m/m or % m/v) must be named.
activities.recall_question: What is the molar mass of ethanoic acid approximately?

activities.subject: chemistry
activities.title: Dissolved oxygen: Winkler-method theory
activities.principle: In the Winkler analytical method dissolved oxygen is related indirectly to a titration through redox stoichiometry.
activities.record_guidance: Study the teacher-provided reaction scheme and supplied data; do not handle hazardous analytical reagents.
activities.analysis_guidance: Interpret dissolved oxygen as a measured water-quality parameter that varies with conditions.
activities.common_error: Dissolved oxygen is not the same as all oxygen chemically bound in water.
activities.recall_question: What does a higher dissolved-oxygen reading generally mean?
activities.recall_answer: More molecular oxygen is present dissolved in that sample, under those conditions.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Vernier calipers: measurement and geometry
activities.principle: A vernier subdivides the main scale; corrected reading = observed reading - signed zero error.
activities.record_guidance: Record main-scale reading, matching vernier division, least count, signed zero error and corrected dimensions.
activities.analysis_guidance: Calculate volumes from corrected dimensions; keep all inputs in one unit before conversion.
activities.common_error: A negative zero error is added on correction, not subtracted twice.
activities.recall_question: What distinguishes precision from accuracy?
activities.recall_answer: Precision concerns the spread of repeated readings; accuracy concerns closeness to an accepted value.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Micrometer screw gauge
activities.principle: Small axial movement per full turn is the pitch; least count usually equals pitch / circular-scale divisions.
activities.record_guidance: Record pitch, least count, main/circular readings, zero error and repeated diameters.
activities.analysis_guidance: Calculate a mean diameter and infer cross-sectional area using A = pi d^2/4.
activities.common_error: The thimble graduation is not a millimetre value without multiplying by least count.
activities.recall_question: Why take readings at different positions?
activities.recall_answer: To detect thickness variation and reduce the effect of random reading error.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Spherometer and radius of curvature
activities.principle: For a spherical surface, R = (l^2 / (6h)) + (h/2), with l the side of the equilateral tripod triangle.
activities.record_guidance: Record instrument zero, three-foot triangle side l, and central screw sagitta h with consistent length units.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compute R and comment on sensitivity when h is small.
activities.common_error: Do not use the triangle's circumradius in place of its side length in this expression.
activities.recall_question: Why is an accurate h crucial?
activities.recall_answer: A small error in h can appreciably affect the calculated curvature radius.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Travelling microscope: precise position
activities.principle: A travelling microscope compares vertical or horizontal position using a vernier scale.
activities.record_guidance: Record successive position readings, least count, zero/reference and differences; note whether measuring depth or displacement.
activities.analysis_guidance: Subtract coordinates rather than treating a coordinate as the required length.
activities.common_error: Do not report apparent depth from a single position reading.
activities.recall_question: What produces a displacement from coordinate readings?
activities.recall_answer: The difference between the final and initial calibrated positions.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Parallelogram of forces and unknown mass
activities.principle: For two forces P and Q with included angle theta, resultant R obeys R^2 = P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ cos(theta).
activities.record_guidance: Record calibrated forces or tensions, angles and equilibrium condition, using class apparatus.
activities.analysis_guidance: Resolve into vector components or a scaled force diagram; relate balancing weight to mg.
activities.common_error: Adding force magnitudes directly is valid only if their directions agree.
activities.recall_question: Why do forces require vector addition?
activities.recall_answer: Both direction and magnitude determine the resultant.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Principle of moments: unknown mass
activities.principle: For equilibrium about a pivot, the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments.
activities.record_guidance: Record masses/weights and perpendicular distances from the pivot; account for any asymmetric beam.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use moment = force x perpendicular distance and solve for unknown weight or mass.
activities.common_error: Do not substitute the length of an oblique arm for its perpendicular lever arm.
activities.recall_question: What is the SI unit of moment?
activities.recall_answer: newton metre (N m).

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Relative density from a U-tube
activities.principle: At the same horizontal level in continuous connected hydrostatic fluids, equilibrium pressures agree.
activities.record_guidance: Record vertical liquid-column heights from the same reference line and the liquid identities.
activities.analysis_guidance: Express density ratio using rho1 h1 = rho2 h2 for appropriate interfaces/equal-level comparison.
activities.common_error: Do not equate heights without identifying which liquid occupies each column.
activities.recall_question: Why use vertical heights rather than tube lengths?
activities.recall_answer: Hydrostatic pressure depends on vertical depth.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Relative density with Hare's apparatus
activities.principle: For each liquid column under the same pressure difference, rho g h has the same value.
activities.record_guidance: Record the two vertical column heights, liquid types and common pressure condition.
activities.analysis_guidance: Find ratio of densities from inverse ratios of corresponding heights.
activities.common_error: A taller column corresponds to lower density for the same pressure difference.
activities.recall_question: If two columns have the same pressure difference, what is rho1/rho2?
activities.recall_answer: h2/h1, provided both heights refer to that common difference.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Density with a weighted test tube
activities.principle: Buoyant force equals the weight of displaced liquid when a floating body is in equilibrium.
activities.record_guidance: Record tube mass and immersion depth in test and reference liquids, including shape information.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate displaced volume to floating equilibrium; compare densities where cross-section is uniform.
activities.common_error: A fixed object's submerged fraction depends on density and tube geometry.
activities.recall_question: What balances weight in a floating equilibrium?
activities.recall_answer: The upthrust from the displaced liquid.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Gravitational acceleration from a simple pendulum
activities.principle: For small amplitudes, T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g), hence T^2 = (4 pi^2/g) L.
activities.record_guidance: Record effective pendulum length and time for several oscillations at different lengths.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot T^2 (s^2) against L (m); slope = 4 pi^2/g, so g = 4 pi^2/slope.
activities.common_error: Timing one swing amplifies reaction-time percentage error.
activities.recall_question: Why keep swing amplitude small?
activities.recall_answer: The simple-harmonic approximation becomes less accurate at large amplitudes.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Loaded spring: mass versus period
activities.principle: For a light spring with effective spring constant k, T^2 = (4 pi^2/k)m under the ideal model.
activities.record_guidance: Record attached mass, oscillation count, total time and period; keep extension within elastic behaviour.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot T^2 against m; gradient gives 4 pi^2/k in the ideal simple model.
activities.common_error: An intercept can reflect effective spring mass and measurement effects.
activities.recall_question: Why graph T^2 rather than T against mass?
activities.recall_answer: T^2 is linearly related to mass in the ideal model.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Sonometer: tuning fork frequency
activities.principle: At fundamental resonance, f = (1/(2L)) sqrt(F/mu), with mu = string mass per unit length.
activities.record_guidance: Record resonant vibrating length, tension, and relevant mass-per-length values.
activities.analysis_guidance: Calculate predicted frequency with consistent units or compare it with a labelled reference fork.
activities.common_error: Do not confuse the suspended hanging mass with the tension force mg.
activities.recall_question: What happens to f when tension quadruples (L and mu fixed)?
activities.recall_answer: Frequency doubles.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Sonometer: frequency versus length
activities.principle: For constant string tension and mass per length, f is proportional to 1/L for fundamental vibration.
activities.record_guidance: Record resonant lengths for labelled fork frequencies at fixed tension.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot f against 1/L; expect an approximately straight-line trend through the origin within errors.
activities.common_error: A plot of frequency against length is inversely curved, not linear.
activities.recall_question: What should be constant in this comparison?
activities.recall_answer: Tension and string linear density.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Closed-tube resonance: one fork and end correction
activities.principle: For a tube closed at one end, consecutive resonances are separated by lambda/2, and f lambda = v.
activities.record_guidance: Record the first and second resonant lengths for the same fork and its frequency.
activities.analysis_guidance: lambda = 2(L2-L1); v = f lambda; end correction e = lambda/4 - L1, in the simple model.
activities.common_error: Using L1 = lambda/4 exactly ignores the open-end correction.
activities.recall_question: Why compare two resonance positions?
activities.recall_answer: The difference eliminates the unknown end correction in lambda.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Closed-tube resonance: several frequencies
activities.principle: At first resonance, L + e = v/(4f), using an effective length correction e.
activities.record_guidance: Record fork frequency f and first resonant length L; note temperature if given.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot L against 1/f; slope v/4 and vertical intercept -e.
activities.common_error: Do not treat L versus f as linear.
activities.recall_question: Which slope gives sound speed from L versus 1/f?
activities.recall_answer: v = 4 x slope (using SI units).

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Glass refractive index: apparent depth
activities.principle: For near-normal viewing from air, n approximately equals real depth / apparent depth.
activities.record_guidance: Record actual block thickness and the apparent displacement from calibrated microscope coordinates.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compute ratio of real to apparent thickness, stating near-normal assumptions.
activities.common_error: The magnification of the microscope is not the refractive index.
activities.recall_question: Why can depth look reduced through glass?
activities.recall_answer: Refraction shifts the apparent position of an object viewed across a boundary.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Prism deviation versus incidence
activities.principle: Prism deviation normally has a minimum as angle of incidence is varied.
activities.record_guidance: Record incidence and deviation pairs from the teacher-supervised optical arrangement.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot deviation against angle of incidence and read minimum deviation from the curve.
activities.common_error: The minimum is not determined by averaging all measured deviations.
activities.recall_question: What characterises the minimum-deviation path?
activities.recall_answer: The ray's path is symmetric inside the prism in the ideal case.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Prism refractive index from critical angle
activities.principle: For a prism-to-air boundary, n = 1/sin C when the other medium is approximately air.
activities.record_guidance: Record the critical angle inferred from labelled ray observations and note the media.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compute n using an angle-mode check on the calculator.
activities.common_error: The refracted ray at critical incidence travels along the boundary.
activities.recall_question: Why is total internal reflection possible only from high to low refractive index?
activities.recall_answer: A critical angle exists only when the incident medium has larger refractive index.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Spectrometer adjustment and prism angle
activities.principle: The prism angle A can be found from the angular separation of reflected telescope images: separation = 2A.
activities.record_guidance: Record both vernier readings for two reflected directions, with circular-angle wrap handled.
activities.analysis_guidance: Find half of the angular difference; compare readings from both sides/verniers where available.
activities.common_error: Do not forget the factor of one-half or mishandle a 0/360 degree crossing.
activities.recall_question: Why use two reflected rays?
activities.recall_answer: Their angular separation is twice the prism's refracting angle.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Spectrometer: minimum deviation and n
activities.principle: For prism angle A and minimum deviation D, n = sin[(A+D)/2] / sin(A/2), in air.
activities.record_guidance: Record both prism angle and minimum-deviation angle from correctly adjusted spectrometer readings.
activities.analysis_guidance: Substitute measured angles and check that n is plausible for the labelled prism material.
activities.common_error: This relation relies on minimum deviation, not arbitrary incidence.
activities.recall_question: What makes the minimum-deviation condition special?
activities.recall_answer: The internal refraction angles are equal in a symmetric ray path.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Convex lens: no-parallax focal length
activities.principle: For real object and image distances as positive magnitudes, 1/f = 1/u + 1/v (thin-lens model).
activities.record_guidance: Record object and real image positions established by no parallax; measure u and v from lens centre.
activities.analysis_guidance: Calculate f = uv/(u+v) using consistent units; compare multiple trials.
activities.common_error: No parallax indicates coincidence of positions, not automatically a sharp image.
activities.recall_question: Why move the eye sideways in a parallax check?
activities.recall_answer: Relative motion reveals whether two images lie in different planes.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Concave lens: no-parallax focal length
activities.principle: A concave (diverging) lens has a negative focal length under the standard Cartesian sign convention.
activities.record_guidance: Record teacher-defined object and virtual image coordinates, keeping the sign convention explicit.
activities.analysis_guidance: Apply the appropriate signed thin-lens equation; explain why the inferred f is negative.
activities.common_error: Blindly using magnitudes in the converging-lens formula gives the wrong sign.
activities.recall_question: What is the sign of focal length for a thin concave lens?
activities.recall_answer: Negative in the standard Cartesian convention.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Atmospheric pressure: quill-tube model
activities.principle: A trapped gas column can illustrate Boyle's law, PV = constant, when temperature remains effectively constant.
activities.record_guidance: Record orientation, trapped-column length and teacher-provided hydrostatic correction quantities.
activities.analysis_guidance: Relate gas pressure to an appropriate pressure-column balance and check reciprocal P-V trend.
activities.common_error: The gas pressure need not equal ambient atmospheric pressure if a liquid column adds head.
activities.recall_question: Which condition is essential for Boyle's law?
activities.recall_answer: Approximately constant temperature and fixed amount of gas.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Gas volume versus absolute temperature
activities.principle: At constant pressure, V is directly proportional to absolute thermodynamic temperature T.
activities.record_guidance: Record T in K and gas volume; label controlled pressure and trapped gas amount.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot V against T (K), expecting a straight-line relation for a near-ideal gas.
activities.common_error: A graph using degrees Celsius has a negative extrapolated intercept, not a Kelvin intercept at -273.
activities.recall_question: Why change Celsius to Kelvin in the ratio V/T?
activities.recall_answer: The gas law uses absolute temperature.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Pressure versus temperature at fixed volume
activities.principle: At constant gas volume and amount, P/T is constant when P is absolute pressure and T in K.
activities.record_guidance: Record given absolute/gauge pressures, temperature and constant-volume condition.
activities.analysis_guidance: Convert gauge to absolute pressure when needed, then plot P_abs versus T.
activities.common_error: Using gauge pressure directly in P/T may invalidate the expected proportionality.
activities.recall_question: Which pressure belongs in the ideal gas law?
activities.recall_answer: Absolute pressure.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Solid heat capacity: mixture method
activities.principle: Ignoring heat loss, heat lost by hot solid equals heat gained by cooler water plus calorimeter.
activities.record_guidance: Record masses, initial temperatures, equilibrium temperature and calorimeter heat capacity if supplied.
activities.analysis_guidance: Write an energy balance before solving c_s; note heat exchange with surroundings.
activities.common_error: Omitting calorimeter heat capacity may bias calculated c_s.
activities.recall_question: Why must temperatures be recorded near mixing time?
activities.recall_answer: Ambient heat exchange changes the energy balance.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Liquid heat capacity by cooling
activities.principle: Under matched cooling conditions, the heat-loss rate is related to effective heat capacity and temperature-fall rate.
activities.record_guidance: Record matched temperature intervals and cooling curves for reference and test liquids.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compare rates at the same temperature difference from surroundings, considering calorimeter contribution.
activities.common_error: Comparing slopes at different excess temperatures ignores changing heat-loss conditions.
activities.recall_question: Why compare cooling rates at the same temperature?
activities.recall_answer: It makes the heat-loss conditions more comparable.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Latent heat of fusion of ice
activities.principle: Melting ice requires latent heat; a calorimetry balance includes ice warming if below 0 C.
activities.record_guidance: Record water/ice masses, temperatures and equilibrium state from supervised experiment.
activities.analysis_guidance: Set heat lost = heat gained; state whether ice is assumed dry and initially at 0 C.
activities.common_error: Surface water adhering to ice biases the estimated fusion latent heat.
activities.recall_question: What is latent heat at the melting point?
activities.recall_answer: Energy absorbed without temperature increase during phase change.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Latent heat of vaporisation of water
activities.principle: Steam condensation releases latent heat and condensed water may cool further to final temperature.
activities.record_guidance: Record steam/condensate mass and initial/final temperatures and calorimeter terms.
activities.analysis_guidance: Construct the full heat balance before extracting latent heat of vaporisation.
activities.common_error: Ignoring cooling of condensate can affect the estimate.
activities.recall_question: Why should condensed steam mass be measured?
activities.recall_answer: It determines the amount of steam whose energy enters the system.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Relative humidity: polished calorimeter
activities.principle: At dew point, the surface becomes saturated; relative humidity is related to saturation vapour pressures.
activities.record_guidance: Record ambient temperature and dew-point temperature from supervised observations.
activities.analysis_guidance: RH (%) = 100 e_s(T_dew)/e_s(T_air) if both saturation vapour pressures are provided.
activities.common_error: RH is not simply 100 x T_dew/T_air.
activities.recall_question: What defines dew point?
activities.recall_answer: Temperature at which water vapour becomes saturated on cooling at nearly constant vapour content.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Thermal conductivity: Searle method
activities.principle: In steady state, axial heat conduction is balanced by heat absorbed in coolant.
activities.record_guidance: Record rod area, separation, rod temperature difference and coolant mass flow/temperature rise.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use k A (dT/dx) = m_dot c deltaT, with temperature gradient along the rod.
activities.common_error: Mixing rod length and area units gives incorrect W m^-1 K^-1.
activities.recall_question: What is the SI unit of thermal conductivity?

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Cell electromotive force and internal resistance
activities.principle: Terminal potential difference obeys V = E - Ir for a cell delivering current.
activities.record_guidance: Record paired current and terminal voltage values for different loads.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot V versus I; intercept E, gradient -r.
activities.common_error: A nonzero current means terminal voltage need not equal E.
activities.recall_question: What does the V-axis intercept represent?
activities.recall_answer: Cell electromotive force E in the linear ideal model.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Copper resistance and temperature coefficient
