activities.principle: Over a moderate temperature interval, R_T = R_ref[1+alpha(T-T_ref)] approximately.
activities.record_guidance: Record bridge balance positions, bath temperature and reference resistance as directed.
activities.analysis_guidance: Find R at each temperature; graph R against T; alpha = slope/R_ref at T_ref.
activities.common_error: The approximation may fail across large ranges or with heating artefacts.
activities.recall_question: What is the SI unit of alpha?

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Potentiometer comparison of two cell EMFs
activities.principle: At null balance with unchanged potentiometer-wire gradient, E1/E2 = l1/l2.
activities.record_guidance: Record balance lengths for the two cells under the same standardised gradient.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compute the ratio of cell EMFs from lengths; null detection limits current through test cell.
activities.common_error: Changing the driving circuit invalidates simple length comparison.
activities.recall_question: Why prefer a null method for comparing EMFs?
activities.recall_answer: Ideally, no current is drawn from the cell being compared at balance.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Internal resistance of a cell: potentiometer
activities.principle: Open-circuit and loaded null lengths satisfy r = R(l_open-l_load)/l_load in the standard model.
activities.record_guidance: Record open-circuit balance length, loaded balance length and external load resistance.
activities.analysis_guidance: Calculate internal resistance and label all assumptions.
activities.common_error: Reverse the numerator and denominator and r becomes incorrect.
activities.recall_question: Which null length is generally longer for a cell delivering current?
activities.recall_answer: The open-circuit EMF length, since terminal p.d. is lower under load.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Forward diode current-voltage relation
activities.principle: An ordinary p-n diode conducts strongly in forward bias after its current increases nonlinearly with applied voltage.
activities.record_guidance: Record measured forward current and voltage in a teacher-provided low-voltage circuit.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot I against V and mark non-ohmic behaviour; do not infer a perfectly fixed switch-on voltage.
activities.common_error: A diode generally does not have a constant resistance over its forward characteristic.
activities.recall_question: Why is its I-V curve non-linear?
activities.recall_answer: Carrier transport changes strongly with forward bias.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Transistor common-emitter transfer characteristic
activities.principle: Over an appropriate active range, collector current changes roughly in proportion to base current, with current gain beta = delta I_C / delta I_B.
activities.record_guidance: Record base and collector currents at a fixed collector-emitter condition, under teacher setup.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot I_C versus I_B and estimate active-region slope.
activities.common_error: Near saturation or cutoff, the active-region gain approximation fails.
activities.recall_question: What does the slope of I_C against I_B estimate?
activities.recall_answer: Incremental common-emitter current gain beta under stated conditions.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Logic gate identification using truth tables
activities.principle: A logic gate maps binary input states to a binary output according to a Boolean operation.
activities.record_guidance: Record each permitted binary input combination and the observed output for authorised low-voltage teaching equipment.
activities.analysis_guidance: Compare the table with AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR as applicable.
activities.common_error: Never identify a gate from only one input-output row.
activities.recall_question: How many input combinations does a two-input gate have?

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Young modulus from extension of steel wire
activities.principle: Within the elastic range, Young modulus E = stress/strain = (F/A)/(deltaL/L).
activities.record_guidance: Record applied force, original wire length, diameter and elastic extension from class data.
activities.analysis_guidance: Plot F versus deltaL where relevant; E = (L/A) x slope.
activities.common_error: Confusing wire diameter with radius multiplies area error by four.
activities.recall_question: What is the unit of Young modulus?
activities.recall_answer: pascal (Pa), equivalent to N m^-2.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Liquid viscosity from laminar capillary flow
activities.principle: For steady laminar flow in an ideal circular capillary, Q = pi r^4 deltaP/(8 eta L).
activities.record_guidance: Record volume collected, collection time, tube radius/length and pressure difference from supervised apparatus.
activities.analysis_guidance: Calculate Q = volume/time; solve for eta only if laminar-flow conditions apply.
activities.common_error: Small error in radius has a large effect because of the fourth power.
activities.recall_question: How does Q change if radius doubles, all else ideal and fixed?
activities.recall_answer: It increases by a factor of 16.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Surface tension from a microscope slide
activities.principle: The force exerted by a liquid contact line depends on surface tension and the effective wetted length.
activities.record_guidance: Record balance-force difference and the wetted contact length or correction specified in class.
activities.analysis_guidance: Use the geometry-specific force balance given by the teacher; justify how many surfaces/contact lines contribute.
activities.common_error: Do not assume one contact line if the geometry contributes two.
activities.recall_question: What is the SI unit of surface tension?

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Surface tension via capillary rise
activities.principle: In an ideal wetting capillary, h = 2 gamma cos(theta)/(rho g r).
activities.record_guidance: Record capillary radius, rise height, density and contact-angle assumption.
activities.analysis_guidance: Estimate gamma = h rho g r/(2 cos theta), using consistent units.
activities.common_error: The contact angle cannot always be assumed exactly zero.
activities.recall_question: What happens to h if capillary radius doubles, all else fixed?
activities.recall_answer: The rise height approximately halves.

activities.subject: physics
activities.title: Surface tension from Jaeger bubble method
activities.principle: The maximum pressure of a bubble forming at a submerged capillary tip includes hydrostatic head and curvature pressure.
activities.record_guidance: Record teacher-supplied bubble pressure data, immersion depth and tip radius.
activities.analysis_guidance: Interpret deltaP_max = rho g h + 2 gamma/r for the idealized single spherical interface near the tip.
activities.common_error: The measured pressure contains hydrostatic contribution; it is not all surface tension.
activities.recall_question: Why subtract the hydrostatic term?
activities.recall_answer: Only the remaining curvature-pressure term is used to estimate gamma.
